ai.title: Refactor live stats polling and add homepage summary
ai.summary: Extracted `useLiveStats`, `countryName`, and `EMPTY_LIVE_STATS` from `live-client.tsx` to new `live-stats-client.ts`. Added `enabled` and `pauseWhenHidden` options to the hook to support visibility-aware polling. New `live-summary.tsx` implements `HomepageLiveStats` using `IntersectionObserver` to trigger updates only when the section is visible. `home-client.tsx` now imports `HomepageLiveStats` instead of `CompactLiveStats`.

eli5.text: When you scroll to the live stats section near the bottom of the freebuff homepage, a richer summary now loads in: a small world map with highlighted countries, a running total of live users, top models, and the last-updated timestamp. The page no longer pings the server for those numbers every minute whether you're looking at them or not, it waits until you've scrolled within roughly 240 pixels of the section, and stops again if you switch tabs or blur the window; if a refresh fumbles, yesterday's numbers stay on screen instead of vanishing. This is live today for every visitor to the homepage, and the older, lighter counter that used to sit in that spot has been taken out. Behind the scenes, the code that fetches and formats those statistics was copied out of the detailed live-stats page.

ai.title: Revert Windows Bun baseline compile target
ai.summary: Reverts Windows Bun compile target from `bun-windows-x64-baseline` to `bun-windows-x64` across CI workflows and build scripts. Removes baseline-specific runtime preparation steps in `cli-release-build.yml`, `freebuff-e2e.yml`, and `npm-app-release-build.yml`. Updates `cli/scripts/build-binary.ts` and `setup-bun-compile-runtime` action to use standard x64 target.

eli5.text: The tool that builds your Windows download stopped using a stripped-down version of the Bun runtime and switched back to the full one, so the Windows release build now runs a standard build step where it previously used a stripped-down mode. If you looked, you would see the release setup label change from the reduced build to the full build in the Windows release flow and the Windows freebuff test flow. This is a behind-the-scenes change to how the Windows build is run, so most readers would not notice it directly unless they watch the build process.

ai.title: Freebuff 1.0.677 release ships live map overhaul CLI model aliases
ai.summary: Freebuff 1.0.677 ships as a release bump in cli/release/package.json, aggregating fixes and features across the CLI, Web, and shared/core surfaces. Highlights include Natural Earth-based live map projection, /model:<mode> slash-command aliases mapping to /mode:<mode> commands, a fix preserving session metadata (accessTier, queueDepthByModel, rateLimitsByModel) when landing from model switches, visibility-aware live stats polling with homepage summaries, terminal-adaptive CLI model selector, Simplified Chinese README, reduced chat request retention via createRequestAuditRecord, skipDisconnectedBilling for DeepSeek V4 Flash, and a revert of Windows Bun build target from baseline back to standard x64. The release covers CLI session hooks, command registry, slash-command data, waiting-room UI, live map rendering, chat completions telemetry, and Web FAQ clarifications on limited mode.
ai.evidence: Commit 147d55f1 modifies cli/release/package.json, changing the version field from 1.0.676 to 1.0.677 (a one-line release bump with +1/-1 stats). The analysis notes confirm this is a release-bump commit that aggregates 11 prior changes across CLI, Web, and shared/core surfaces, including model switch fixes, live map overhaul, Chinese README, CLI slash-command model aliases, connected stream billing, terminal-adaptive model selector, live stats homepage summary, and a Windows Bun target revert.

eli5.text: Freebuff 1.0.677 makes the AI coding assistant more accessible and informative, especially for users in limited access regions. The release adds a live global map showing where other users are building, now drawn with accurate geography instead of rough shapes, and the homepage shows quick stats that update only when you're looking at them. Users can now type /model:<mode> as a shortcut instead of /mode:<mode>, and the /model command also lets you jump straight to the model picker when ending a session. The waiting room for limited users now explains exactly why access is restricted (like using a VPN or being in an unsupported country) instead of showing a generic message. On small terminal windows, the model selector automatically rearranges itself so nothing gets cut off or squished. For privacy, the system stops logging your actual chat messages and instead records only a summary, and it cancels unused AI response streams so you don't accidentally consume credits while disconnected.

ai.title: Freebuff 0.0.91 release ships live map overhaul, CLI model aliases
ai.summary: This release bump in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` aggregates a day of user-facing work: the live map now renders from accurate Natural Earth geometry with an Equal Earth projection (web `/live`), CLI users get `/model:<mode>` slash-command aliases mapping to `/mode:<mode>` plus `/model` on end-session, and session metadata like `accessTier` / `queueDepthByModel` is preserved across model switches. Additional changes reduce chat request retention via `createRequestAuditRecord` (omitting message bodies for `limited` tiers), add `skipDisconnectedBilling` for DeepSeek V4 Flash, make the CLI model selector terminal-height adaptive, ship a Simplified Chinese README, and clarify limited-mode messaging both on the web FAQ and in the CLI waiting room.
ai.evidence: The commit modifies `freebuff/cli/release/package.json`, changing the `version` field from `0.0.90` to `0.0.91`. This is a release-bump commit (commit nature: release-bump) with only +1/-1 stats, aggregating the same-day user-visible fixes and improvements listed in the release instructions.

eli5.text: Freebuff 0.0.91 brings a sharper, more realistic live world map to the web dashboard, a fully translated Simplified Chinese README, and new /model aliases so you can switch AI models in the CLI using either /model:<mode> or /mode:<mode> interchangeably. The homepage now shows compact live stats that refresh every 60 seconds instead of every 15, reducing battery and bandwidth use, while the CLI model picker automatically shrinks its ASCII logo and adds scroll-friendly layout math so it stays usable on short terminal windows. Behind the scenes, the developers also tightened privacy by stopping full chat message bodies from being logged for limited-access users, and they improved billing accuracy by canceling streams faster when a DeepSeek V4 Flash response is interrupted. Upgrading gives you a cleaner, faster, and more language-friendly experience whether you are checking the live map, picking models in the terminal, or just reading the docs in Chinese.

ai.title: Clarify global availability in FAQ
ai.summary: Updated the FAQ answer in freebuff/web/src/app/home-client.tsx to state that Freebuff is available in all countries, operating in either 'full' or 'limited' mode. This change clarifies that while full access is restricted to a specific list of countries, the service remains accessible globally with limited functionality.

eli5.text: If you visit Freebuff's website, the FAQ section now states clearly that the service is available in all countries, not just the full list named there, since the service operates globally in 'full' or 'limited' mode. You would notice the wording changed from implying a hard block outside those countries to explicitly confirming worldwide access with reduced functionality. This clarification affects anyone outside the named countries (or using a VPN) who previously may have wondered whether the service worked where they were.

ai.title: Fix Freebuff 429 error messaging in CLI
ai.summary: The CLI now intercepts HTTP 429 rate-limit errors for Freebuff, displaying a friendly 'temporarily busy' message instead of raw API details. This is implemented via `getFreebuffRateLimitErrorMessage` in `cli/src/utils/error-handling.ts`, which checks for `statusCode === 429` and preserves specific `free_mode_rate_limited` messages if present. The fix applies to both `handleRunCompletion` and `handleRunError` in `cli/src/hooks/helpers/send-message.ts`, gated by `IS_FREEBUFF`. Documentation in `docs/error-schema.md` is updated to reflect this new error handling path.

eli5.text: If you're using the Freebuff version of the assistant and you hit it too hard, it now tells you 'temporarily busy, please wait' instead of flashing a confusing error code. This only happens when the rate-limit kicks in, and it applies specifically to the Freebuff build, regular users won't see it. You'd notice it as a clean, friendly message replacing what used to look like a raw server complaint.

ai.title: Clarify limited mode reason text in CLI waiting room
ai.summary: Updated getLimitedModeReason in cli/src/components/waiting-room-screen.tsx to display 'based on detected country: <code>' instead of 'outside available countries (<code>)' for country_not_allowed errors. The change improves clarity on why access is restricted based on geolocation. Formatting adjustments were also applied to PRIVACY_SIGNAL_LABELS and selectorMaxHeight calculations.

eli5.text: When someone tries to use the tool from a country where access isn't allowed, they will now see a clearer message that says their access was restricted because of their detected country, along with the country code. Previously, the message just said "outside available countries" without as much explanation. This only affects the text shown during the waiting-room screen, and it is live now.

ai.title: Freebuff 0.0.92 ships global availability FAQ, 429 messaging
ai.summary: The Freebuff CLI package version was bumped from 0.0.91 to 0.0.92 in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json`, packaging the three same-day commits that shipped alongside this release: the FAQ now states Freebuff is available globally in full or limited mode, the CLI intercepts HTTP 429 rate-limit failures with a friendly 'temporarily busy' message via `getFreebuffRateLimitErrorMessage` in `cli/src/utils/error-handling.ts`, and `getLimitedModeReason` in `cli/src/components/waiting-room-screen.tsx` now shows 'based on detected country: <code>' for country_not_allowed errors. These changes land in the `freebuff/CLI` packaging surface and carry forward into Web/Desktop through the shared provider catalog and error schema documented in `docs/error-schema.md`.
ai.evidence: The diff modifies `freebuff/cli/release/package.json`, changing the `"version"` field from `"0.0.91"` to `"0.0.92"`; the commit metadata and analysis notes confirm this is a release-bump whose shipped contents are the three preceding same-day commits (FAQ global-availability clarification, CLI 429 messaging fix, CLI limited-mode reason-text clarification).

eli5.text: Freebuff 0.0.92 improves clarity and user experience around global access and rate limiting. The FAQ now clearly states that Freebuff is available in all countries, operating in either full or limited mode depending on location. When the service is temporarily overloaded, you will now see a friendly error message like temporarily busy instead of confusing technical details about rate limits. The waiting room screen, shown when access is restricted due to your location, now gives a clearer explanation stating based on detected country instead of outside available countries. These changes make the software more transparent and easier to understand when you encounter access restrictions or temporary service delays.

ai.title: Remove redundant live stats copy
ai.summary: Stripped `sublabel` and descriptive paragraph from `HomepageLiveStats` in `live-summary.tsx`. Removed static text to reduce visual noise. Scope: Web live stats UI only.

eli5.text: The live stats display on the homepage no longer shows extra text under each country and model name. It also removes the explanatory sentence below the big number that counted active sessions right now. If you open the live page today, the numbers are still there but surrounded by less clutter.
